# `silk/time/now`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The present moment as each `silk.time` type: [`Now`](#Now) reads the `SystemClock` effect and, for
local values, a `Zone`.

## When to use

Use it where code needs today's date or the time now. Each function shows in its signature
what it reads: the clock, and for the zone of the machine also `LocalZone` and `TimeZones`.
A test provides a fixed clock and `FixedLocalZone`, and the result is the same on every
machine.

## Details

There is no local time without a zone. Load the zone one time with [`Now.localZone`](#Now.impl.localZone) or
`TimeZones.zone`, keep it, and pass it to [`Now.zonedIn`](#Now.impl.zonedIn), [`Now.dateIn`](#Now.impl.dateIn), or
[`Now.dateTimeIn`](#Now.impl.dateTimeIn).

## Examples

### Today's date in a zone

```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.system.system_clock { SystemClock }
import silk.system.system_clock_native { OsSystemClock }
import silk.time.now { Now }
import silk.time.offset { UtcOffset }
import silk.time.zone { Zone }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut clock = OsSystemClock.make()
  let tokyo = Zone.fixed(UtcOffset.fromMinutes(540))
  let today = run Now.dateIn(&tokyo) |> Effect.provideMut<SystemClock>(&mut clock)
  if today.year() < 2026 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Now` with `import silk.time.now { Now }`.

<a id="Now.impl.localZone"></a>

### Associated function `localZone`

```silk
pub effect fn localZone() -> Zone
    ! NoLocalZoneError | ZoneLookupError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut LocalZone | &mut TimeZones | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the zone that the machine is set to: the name from `LocalZone`, and its rules from
`TimeZones`.

#### Errors

- `NoLocalZoneError` if the machine does not say which zone it is in.
- `ZoneLookupError` if the `TimeZones` provider does not have that zone.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the zone.
